items.title: How Binance’s $6.3 Billion Hack Went Down
items.author: David Yaffe-Bellany
items.content: <article>A war room. A global conference call. A founder who live-posted about the largest crypto heist in history. Inside a frantic 24 hours at the world’s biggest crypto exchange.</article>

items.title: In San Francisco’s A.I. Boom, a First Date Has Become an Interview
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>When there is A.I. to build, who has time for romance? Techies are going out less and expecting more on each date — including a family health history.</article>

items.title: Big Tech’s Data Center Blitz Is Burning Through Cash and Scaring Wall St.
items.author: Karen Weise
items.content: <article>Amazon became the latest tech company to announce swelling investments in A.I. amid stumbling share prices.</article>

items.title: Hack Could Leave AO3, a Popular Fan Fiction Site, Offline for Weeks
items.author: Rebecca Chao
items.content: <article>AO3, which hosts 18 million stories spun off from the likes of “Harry Potter” and “Heated Rivalry,” was taken offline after “an intrusion,” one of its founders said.</article>

items.title: Polymarket and Kalshi Face a Major Accuracy Test: The Midterms
items.author: Stuart A. Thompson
items.content: <article>Studies have shown that the betting sites can predict races correctly, but their ability to forecast U.S. midterm elections is an important proving ground.</article>

items.title: Binance’s $6.3 Billion Hack Is Just the Start of a Risky New Era
items.author: David Yaffe-Bellany and Dustin Volz
items.content: <article>The largest cyber heist in history came as attackers increasingly use artificial intelligence and other advanced techniques to steal crypto and quickly launder the funds.</article>

items.title: House Democrats Criticize Justice Dept. Support of OpenAI in Copyright Suit
items.author: Karen Weise
items.content: <article>In a court filing, top Democrats on the Judiciary Committee indicated their support for publishers in a lawsuit led by The New York Times.</article>

items.title: You Can See Everything That Billy Evans Watched on 2x Speed
items.author: C.J. Robinson
items.content: <article>What was Elizabeth Holmes’s partner watching in the new Nathan Fielder documentary? We found the videos (and the scientists in them).</article>

items.title: Binance Suspends Withdrawals After Crypto Hackers Steal $6.3 Billion
items.author: David Yaffe-Bellany and Ryan Mac
items.content: <article>The crypto exchange said it was compromised in what could be the biggest crypto heist ever. One research lab attributed the theft to “North Korea’s elite hacking unit.”</article>

items.title: This Device Uses A.I. and Lasers to Kill Mosquitoes
items.author: Keith Bradsher, Nailah Morgan, Qilai Shen and Siyi Zhao
items.content: <article>A Chinese start-up has developed a device that uses artificial intelligence and lasers to kill mosquitoes. But there are safety concerns for people and other creatures nearby when the device is in action.</article>

items.title: Are We in an A.I. Bubble? We’re About to Find Out.
items.author: Max Read, Whitney Jones, Sawyer Roque, Vjeran Pavic, Daniel Ramirez, Dan Powell, Marion Lozano and Alyssa Moxley
items.content: <article>“This is the first pure-play L.L.M. company to go public, to open its books so we can actually look at the underlying business of this A.I. boom.”</article>

items.title: Intel’s Shares Plunge 20% as A.I. Hinders Some Parts of Its Business
items.author: Don Clark
items.content: <article>The chipmaker, whose largest investor is the U.S. government, reported that the A.I. boom’s domino effect had hurt sales to personal computer makers.</article>

items.title: Polymarket and Kalshi Turn Midterm Elections Into a Multimillion Dollar Market
items.author: Stuart A. Thompson and Lauren McCarthy
items.content: <article>Betting markets like Polymarket and Kalshi have transformed America’s democracy into a new kind of casino.</article>

items.title: DoorDash to Buy Instacart for $17 Billion, Uniting 2 Delivery Giants
items.author: Emmy Martin and Lauren McCarthy
items.content: <article>The deal combines the country’s largest restaurant delivery service with its biggest online grocery platform.</article>

items.title: Microsoft’s Profit Jumps 32% Despite Big Increase in Spending
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>The company’s free cash flow stayed positive in the last quarter even as it spent $45.2 billion on capital expenses like data centers and offered to pay workers to leave.</article>

items.title: Bodacious A.I. Bots Are Stealing Jokes From Young Female Comedians
items.author: Jason Zinoman
items.content: <article>Swiping jokes word for word, these bodacious bots mainly lift from young female comedians. What’s so insidious is how they’re subtly changing us, the audience.</article>

items.title: Hit the Road This Season With These Useful New Map Features
items.author: J. D. Biersdorfer
items.content: <article>The recent updates to Google Maps and Apple’s Maps use artificial (and human) intelligence for better navigation, planning and travel guides.</article>

items.title: Alphabet’s Revenue Rises 25% as Profit Falls
items.author: Kate Conger
items.content: <article>The company has been spending relentlessly to build A.I. and said it would increase those investments next year. Profit dropped because of changes to the value of its investments.</article>

items.title: AI Is Finding a Flood of Bugs, and Silicon Valley Is Rushing to Fix Them
items.author: Kate Conger
items.content: <article>A.I. has uncovered a horde of software flaws, which engineers are racing to fix before they can be exploited and abused by hackers.</article>

items.title: Apple Unveils Its First Touch-Screen MacBook Pro
items.author: Kalley Huang and Brian X. Chen
items.content: <article>Steve Jobs and Tim Cook both dismissed the idea, but Apple’s new chief executive is reimagining some of the company’s most important products.</article>

items.title: Wanted: Robot-Dog Walkers. $20/Hour.
items.author: Kashmir Hill
items.content: <article>No pooper scooper required.</article>

items.title: GM Is Leaving NYSE for the Nasdaq After More Than 100 Years
items.author: Aruni Soni
items.content: <article>After more than 100 years on the New York Stock Exchange, the automaker is shifting its listing to the Nasdaq, which is home to many technology companies.</article>

items.title: How Billionaires Are Fighting the Prop 40 California Wealth Tax
items.author: Theodore Schleifer and Erin Griffith
items.content: <article>The latest Silicon Valley billionaire club is a $333 million political ad machine that is heavily engaged in next week’s elections.</article>

items.title: In the A.I. ‘Robogym,’ Machines Train to Be More Like Humans
items.author: James Paton
items.content: <article>Germany’s Neura is one of the companies at the forefront of efforts to use artificial intelligence in robotics, and crucial to whether Europe can close the gap with China.</article>

items.title: The Key Numbers From Anthropic’s IPO Filing
items.author: Sri Muppidi and Lauren Hirsch
items.content: <article>We broke down the A.I. company’s key figures, which give insight into the health of its business, its future plans and who’s in charge.</article>

items.title: Microsoft Offers Buyouts to 60,000 Employees as It Spends on A.I.
items.author: Karen Weise
items.content: <article>About a quarter of the tech giant’s employees were eligible for the packages, although the company cautioned it did not expect many employees to sign on.</article>

items.title: Anthropic’s IPO S-1 Spells Out a Future of Promise and Peril
items.author: Mike Isaac
items.content: <article>The A.I. company took great pains to describe the many benefits that can come from using its Claude chatbot and technology, but also offered up a heavy dose of gloom.</article>

items.title: What’s Riding on Anthropic Going Public? Nearly Everything.
items.author: Erin Griffith and Lauren Hirsch
items.content: <article>Anthropic sits atop a pyramid of business partners and suppliers, making it a barometer of the broader economy. Its initial public offering will have widespread implications.</article>

items.title: Anthropic S-1 Reveals Rapid Growth Ahead of Blockbuster IPO
items.author: Mike Isaac, Erin Griffith, Lauren Hirsch and Sri Muppidi
items.content: <article>Ahead of what could be the largest public listing ever, Anthropic said revenue soared to $16.3 billion in the first half of the year, and it planned to spend $807 billion on A.I. infrastructure.</article>

items.title: Meet Anthropic’s Seven Founders as the A.I. Firm Prepares for an IPO
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>Former OpenAI employees started the company in 2021 after disagreements over how to safely build artificial intelligence. An I.P.O. could make them billionaires.</article>

items.title: Darline Graham Gets Help From the Data Center Industry in South Carolina Senate Race
items.author: Theodore Schleifer and Emily Davies
items.content: <article>As political fights over artificial intelligence accelerate, there is now a super PAC aligned with the data center industry. Its first bet is on Ms. Graham, a Republican in an unexpectedly tight race.</article>

items.title: Put Your A.I. Agents to Work with These 5 Killer Tasks
items.author: Brian X. Chen
items.content: <article>When you start using Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s dots for these tasks — like applying for jobs and booking hard-to-get restaurant tables — you may never go back.</article>
